title: Japanese woodblock prints
examples: How did Japanese prints affect European art?

explain.say: Today we will learn about ukiyo-e prints. These prints were very popular in Japan. They showed scenes from everyday life.

items: Ukiyo-e means 'pictures of the floating world'
They depicted common people and scenes

explain.say: A famous artist was Katsushika Hokusai. He created many beautiful prints. One of his most famous works is The Great Wave.
The Great Wave captures a dramatic moment. It shows a large wave approaching the shore. This print is a masterpiece of Japanese art.
These Japanese prints influenced European artists greatly. Artists in Europe started copying the style. This is called Japonisme.
Think about a modern comic book. The panel layouts and action shots are similar. They tell a story visually, just like these prints.
A common mistake is thinking all Japanese art is woodblock prints. Remember that Japanese art includes many other forms too. Paintings and pottery are also important.

draw.text: Mistake: Not all Japanese art is prints

faq.a: Ukiyo-e translates to 'pictures of the floating world'. It refers to the culture and transient pleasures of the Edo period.
asks: What is the meaning of ukiyo-e?
Can you explain the term ukiyo-e?

faq.q: Who was the most famous artist associated with these prints?
faq.a: Katsushika Hokusai is one of the most famous artists. He is best known for his series including The Great Wave.

faq.q: How did these prints reach Europe?
faq.a: They reached Europe through international trade routes. This exposure led to a major artistic movement called Japonisme.
asks: Why did European artists start using this style?

faq.q: Were these prints made by hand or printed?
faq.a: They were created using a woodblock printing process. An artist would draw, and others would carve and print the image.

faq.q: Are there other famous Japanese prints besides The Great Wave?
faq.a: Yes, artists like Utamaro specialized in portraits. They captured famous actors and beautiful women of the time.

facts: Ukiyo-e prints were popular in Japan during the Edo period.
Hokusai's series 'Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji' features The Great Wave.
The style's influence on Europe is known as Japonisme.
The prints were created using carved woodblocks.

quiz.say: The style of art that shows scenes from everyday life in Japan is called:
quiz.why: Ukiyo-e literally means pictures of the floating world, describing daily life scenes.

wrong.1: This is the name for the influence in Europe, not the Japanese art style itself.
wrong.2: This describes the medium used to create the print, not the name of the art style.
wrong.3: This is the name of a very famous artist, not the name of the art genre.

quiz.say: Which artist is famous for the print titled The Great Wave?
quiz.why: Hokusai is the artist credited with creating this iconic and dramatic piece.

wrong.0: Utamaro was another famous artist, but he specialized in different subjects.
wrong.1: This is the subject matter the art depicts, not the creator.
wrong.2: This term relates to the impact of the art in other countries.

quiz.say: The European adoption of Japanese art styles is best described by the term:
quiz.why: Japonisme is the specific term used to describe the strong influence of Japanese art on Western art.

wrong.0: This is the literal meaning of the art's subject, not the historical term for the influence.
wrong.2: This is the original Japanese name for the prints, not the name of the influence.
wrong.3: This refers to the physical method of printing, not the art movement.
